physical.notes: Width, height, depth and weight are the docs page's product size (48.0 x 24.0 x 8.4 mm) and product weight (17.0 g); the package is 104.4 x 65.0 x 18.0 mm and 25.3 g gross. The vendor's own dimension drawing of the SE (K016-P-SE model size) dimensions the case 13.52 mm deep, the depth measurements.json uses; the 8.4 mm of the docs page matches no dimension on that drawing. The enclosure is translucent orange with a magnetic back.

specs.cpu: Xtensa dual-core 32-bit LX6, up to 240 MHz
specs.in_package_other: crystal oscillator, filter capacitors, SPI flash and RF matching circuit
specs.gpio: up to 34, 5 of them strapping pins
specs.chip_revision: v1.0 or v1.1 (Espressif upgraded the ESP32 die from v1.0 to v1.1, PCN20220901); v1.1 on the unit measured
specs.supply_net: VESP_3V3 on VDDA (pins 1, 43, 46), VDD3P3_CPU (37) and VDDA3P3 (3), decoupled by C38, C39, C41, C42 (100 nF each) and C44 (10 uF). VDD3P3_RTC (19) and VDDA3P3 (4) are drawn on their own nets with C40 and C43 (100 nF): their wires cross the VESP_3V3 bar with no junction dot. Pin 19 is certainly supplied, since VDD_SDIO, the in-package flash's supply, is powered from it (the MTDI strap reads low at reset); neither pin's rail is settled (schematic/README.md, Open questions)
specs.vdd_sdio: pin 26, not connected on the board: the in-package flash's supply, powered from VDD3P3_RTC rather than the internal 1.8 V LDO because the MTDI strap (IO12, pin 18, unconnected, internal pull-down) reads low at reset, unless the eFuse EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE overrides it
specs.unconnected_gpio: IO4, IO12, IO14 and IO19 reach nothing on the board; IO6, IO7, IO8, IO11, IO16 and IO17 are the in-package flash's lines (Espressif's Table 3), crossed out on the schematic because nothing outside the package uses them
specs.strapping_pins: GPIO0 (internal pull-up, R12 1 kOhm up), GPIO2 (internal pull-down), MTDI/IO12 (internal pull-down), MTDO/IO15 (LCD_MOSI, internal pull-up), GPIO5 (LCD_CS, internal pull-up)
specs.input_only_gpio: GPIO34 to GPIO39, with no internal pulls; no resistor on the board pulls GPIO36 (pad PAD4) or GPIO38 (pad PAD3); whether GPIO25 meets GPIO36 at the Hat-Bus header is not yet measured

pins.LNA_IN (pin 2): E1 through a pi network: C2 1.5 pF to GND, L1 1.8 nH series, C1 1.2 pF to GND

connects_to.notes: ESP32_EN is also driven by the AXP192's PWROK and by the USB bridge's reset switch (MOS2); GPIO0 also reaches the microphone clock, the boot switch (MOS1) and pad PAD5. No pull is drawn on GPIO2.

components.notes: The schematic leaves the module's designator unassigned ("U?", value PICO_D4). The chip revision v1.1 was read from the one SE unit the Kleidos project has; the docs page lists only "2.4 GHz Wi-Fi" and does not mention Bluetooth, which comes from Espressif's datasheet.
Espressif's datasheet does not name the flash die.

components.notes: One chip holds the board's charger, fuel gauge and four of its five rails (DCDC1, LDO1, LDO2, LDO3, LDOio0); the fifth, the 5 V EXT_VDD, is the SGM6603 boost it enables. The docs page's power map agrees: LDO1 = RTC_VDD, LDO2 = LCD_BL, LDO3 = LCD_LOGIC_VCC, GPIO0 = MIC_VCC, EXT_EN = Grove 5 V boost enable, PWRON = power key. VBUS_VIN and VBUS_USB accept 4.8-5.5 V, and with VBUS present the AXP192 charges the battery (docs page).

notes: Nets and their sources: VESP_3V3 is the AXP192's DCDC1 output and supplies the SoC, every pull-up and both LEDs; IPSOUT is the AXP192's Intelligent Power Select output, which feeds its own converters, the SGM6603 boost and R401; EXT_VDD is the 5 V boost output on the Grove port and PAD7; VBUS_USB comes from the USB-C port and VBUS_VIN from PAD6 (VIN). The schematic is one A4 sheet, drawn from the StickC-Plus V1.1's with the IMU footprint left unfitted. Pin numbers are the schematic's symbol pins.

bench-gpio27.title: GPIO27 and the AXP192 N_VBUSEN on the Kleidos bench unit of the StickC-Plus SE (Kleidos boards bench record m5stickc-plus-se/schematic/bench/2026-11-17-gpio27-n-vbusen.md)
bench-gpio27.method: Over the board's USB-C port, case closed, battery fitted: GPIO27 driven high and released from a bench-only debug build (never committed), with REG00H, the VBUS current ADC and the battery current ADCs read 25 times in each state.

bench-gpio2.title: GPIO2 load and tone on the Kleidos bench unit of the StickC-Plus SE (Kleidos boards bench record m5stickc-plus-se/schematic/bench/2026-11-17-gpio2-buzzer.md)
bench-gpio2.method: Over the board's USB-C port, case closed: a 2.7 kHz LEDC tone and static levels on GPIO2 from a bench-only debug build (never committed), the AXP192's VBUS current averaged over 30-40 reads per state, and GPIO2's level read after release with no pull; nobody listened.
